trusted: The coordinator instantiates and invokes only the exact reviewed bootstrap after all three exact GO receipts are committed in A.
Git object bytes are content-addressed and every read sets GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1.
Pinned host executables match their recorded SHA-256 values and implement their documented interfaces.
The local Docker daemon, host kernel, and digest-bound image report truthful create, inspect, exit, cgroup, and cleanup state.
Receipt principal authenticity is supplied by the multi-agent orchestrator; the validator proves syntax, exclusion, distinction, role, topology, and digest bindings.
excluded: A malicious concurrent process under the same uid after bootstrap begins.
Intentional deletion or rewriting of the consumption/result refs, reflogs, Git objects, or authorization history.
Compromise of Docker, the host kernel, Git/hash implementations, pinned executables, or the multi-agent orchestrator.
model.dirty_worktree_boundary: Tracked or untracked worktree changes outside the run directory are not executable/input bytes because every such byte is read from exact commits. V12 deliberately does not invoke git status or any worktree-to-index content conversion. The repository, experiments directory, and experiment directory must each be a nonsymlink directory whose physical path equals its configured path; forbidden sidecar/cache names in the experiment scope and three ancestor literals still reject.
model.post_run_custody: Run-directory files remain mutable, but the result ref immutably binds the exact artifact manifest and canonical result seal. Later mutation is detectable unless the no-ref/object-rewrite assumption is violated.

rules: P is cleanly committed with sole parent expected_parent_commit_sha1 and the exact recursive raw delta above.
All four additions are regular blobs at mode 100644 and match their bound SHA-256 values.
The inherited container runner and protected source/test remain byte-identical and are not parsed, imported, compiled, or executed during review.

authorization_chain.required_topology: base -> P -> A; consumption ref -> C with sole parent A; result ref -> R with sole parent C
rules: Before Docker create, C contains only canonical consumption.json, has sole parent A, and is installed directly at the nonsymbolic consumption ref by update-ref --no-deref from the all-zero old value.
The runner assigns and recovers C from the authoritative ref immediately after CAS success; candidate and observed IDs are status-checked artifacts.

R contains exactly artifact-manifest.sha256 and canonical result-seal.json, has sole parent C, and is installed directly at the nonsymbolic result ref by a second update-ref --no-deref all-zero-old-value CAS. Normal completion and the footer perform full recovery. Signal handling only observes the exact 41-byte loose R ref and reports RESULT_PRESENT_UNVALIDATED, never an R-absent incomplete state.
The branch remains at A. Archive input is addressed by exact A; C and R are receipt objects only.
Ordinary replay fails on the existing run directory or consumption ref. Deleting refs/objects is outside the model and forbidden.

runner_script_lines: git_safe() { /opt/homebrew/bin/gtimeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=5s 30s /usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 /usr/bin/git -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -C "$repo" "$@"; }

for path in "$repo" "${repo}/experiments" "${repo}/${exp}"; do [[ -d "$path" && ! -L "$path" ]] || exit 72; physical=$(cd -q -- "$path" && pwd -P) || exit 72; [[ "$physical" == "$path" ]] || exit 72; done

git_safe show "${a}:${host_path}" | /opt/homebrew/bin/gtimeout --verbose --signal=TERM --kill-after=60s 420s /usr/bin/env -i HOME=/tmp TMPDIR=/tmp LANG=C LC_ALL=C PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin DOCKER_HOST=unix:///var/run/docker.sock /bin/zsh -f -s -- launch "$a" "$p" "$protocol_sha" "$host_sha" "$auth_validator_sha" "$container_sha" "$result_validator_sha"
canonical_bootstrap.instantiation_rule: Join runner_script_lines with LF and one terminal LF. Replace every token exactly once with the lowercase digest committed in A. Reject residue, extra substitution, alternate cwd, environment, prefix, suffix, or argv.
canonical_bootstrap.pretrust_rule: No git status, diff-files, hash-object without --no-filters, checkout, add, or worktree-content conversion is permitted. Effective local/worktree filter commands, tar.<format>.command keys, and info/attributes are rejected before the hash-verified host blob executes.
canonical_bootstrap.time_rule: Each pretrust Git operation has a 30-second limit and 5-second grace. The verified host process, including setup, authorization, consumption, Docker lifecycle, finalization, and sealing, has one aggregate 420-second limit and 60-second grace. Signal/EXIT create-pending Docker recovery uses 4-second operations with 1-second per-operation grace.

physical_inventory.type_rule: Every matching filesystem object is rejected regardless of regular-file, directory, or symlink type.
physical_inventory.rule: Every find status is checked. Each recorded phase includes the entire experiment scope plus all ancestor literals. Before run-directory creation, every configured directory component is a nonsymlink directory with exact physical ancestry. Final artifact enumeration uses zsh pathname arrays including dot entries, rejects newline names and every object type except nonsymlink regular files/directories, and therefore does not serialize filenames through newline-delimited discovery.

host_runner.container_name_rule: Exact container name is container_name_prefix concatenated with the already-known 40-hex protocol commit P passed by the bootstrap. Authorization commit A remains independently bound in exact Docker labels, authorization receipts, C, and R; A is not embedded in any blob used to construct A.
host_runner.consumption_ref_precondition: absent and not a direct or dangling symbolic ref
host_runner.result_ref_precondition: absent and not a direct or dangling symbolic ref

global_file_limit.scope: All host-runner file writes, including setup, Docker inspect/logs, protected pipeline, receipts, and manifests.

resource_accounting.protected_pipeline: time -lp covers exact-A archive, tee, Docker attach, and protected execution; cgroup before/after JSON covers integral CPU, memory, and PID counters.
resource_accounting.fixed_overhead: Not charged as cryptanalytic work. The full controller including result sealing is wall-bounded by the external aggregate timeout and file-bounded globally. preseal_host_elapsed_seconds ends when the canonical run receipt begins and therefore includes authorization, consumption, Docker setup/execution/cleanup, and final forbidden-name inventory, but excludes manifest construction, result-object construction, and result-ref CAS.
resource_accounting.interpretation: No relation-generation, scaling, batch, memory-bandwidth, rho, or ECDLP cost claim is authorized.

input_transport.method: git archive at exact A through tee to exact-ID Docker stdin
input_transport.filter_boundary: No effective local/worktree clean/process/smudge filter or tar.<format>.command is available. Any remaining attribute-based archive byte transformation still fails the in-container runner/source/test digest checks before import.

host_runner.canonical_authorization_rule: Each receipt and the decision must be exactly one LF-terminated jq -cS object. Byte comparison occurs before semantic validation, rejecting duplicate keys and noncanonical numeric forms. UUID and hexadecimal syntax checks also bind exact lengths and strict \z anchors, so encoded trailing line feeds cannot evade identity or exclusion checks.
host_runner.canonical_terminal_output_rule: Every JSON-bearing terminal classification requires stdout.json to be exactly one LF-terminated jq -cS value before semantic classification. Duplicate keys, extra JSON values, alternate whitespace/key order, and noncanonical numeric forms therefore classify as infrastructure failure rather than TEST_FAILURE, PREFLIGHT_FAILURE, or VALID_DEVELOPMENT_TEST. Result identities, hashes, and timestamps use exact lengths and strict \z anchors.
host_runner.valid_artifact_rule: VALID_DEVELOPMENT_TEST requires the exact hard-coded regular-file set and sole evidence-input subdirectory. Every dot entry is included in enumeration; every symlink, FIFO, socket, device, newline-containing name, extra file, or extra directory rejects. Complete hashes, exact final empty forbidden-name inventory, canonical receipt/seal, proved cleanup, successful result-ref CAS, and authoritative R recovery are mandatory.

incomplete_predicates.preconsumption_failure: run directory exists and consumption ref is absent; protected execution did not begin
incomplete_predicates.incomplete_infrastructure_failure: consumption ref exists and result ref is absent
incomplete_predicates.sealed_terminal_result: result ref exists; its canonical result-seal classification and bound artifact manifest are authoritative
incomplete_predicates.result_present_unvalidated: the exact 41-byte loose result ref is visible during signal/footer handling, but full R validation did not finish; exit 76 is neither sealed success nor R-absent incomplete
incomplete_predicates.consumption_present_unvalidated: the exact 41-byte loose consumption ref is visible before in-process recovery completed; exit 77 is neither preconsumption nor a sealed result

host_runner.incomplete_process_exit: INCOMPLETE_INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE is never accepted in R. It is only the host exit classification when validated C exists and no exact loose R is visible. Exit 76 reports visible unvalidated R; exit 77 reports visible unvalidated C. Neither transitional state is accepted in R or promoted without independent full recovery.

container.creation: CREATE_PENDING is set before docker create. Docker stdout and cidfile are written directly to regular files before extraction. Direct adoption requires create status zero, stdout byte-exact 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters plus one LF (65 bytes), cidfile byte-exact the same 64 characters with no LF (64 bytes), and matching extracted IDs. While pending, signal and EXIT cleanup use separately 4-second-bounded deterministic-name inspect, adopt only an exact ID/name/A/C-label match, remove only by adopted ID, and prove both ID and name absent. Every failed, missing, single-source, contaminated, or mismatched acknowledgement is cleaned and rejected before start.
container.name_boundary: Name is used only for recovery inspect and final absence verification, never for start or removal.

security_projection.claim: Exact security-critical projection only, not exact whole Docker JSON objects.
includes: exact ID, name, image, hostname, user, entrypoint, command, stdin/stdout/stderr flags, environment multiset/cardinality, healthcheck, labels, volumes and mounts
network, ports, DNS, extra hosts, links, namespaces, runtime, OOM policy, privilege, devices, capabilities, no-new-privileges, readonly root and proc masks
memory, no-swap, CPU, PIDs, nofile/fsize, tmpfs, shm, UID/GID, cgroup and mount runtime attestations
security_projection.unclaimed: Unlisted Docker inspect defaults have no exactness claim.

container.cleanup_rule: Before any R, deterministic-name inspect must return status 1 with stdout byte-exact [] plus one LF and stderr byte-exact Error: No such object: <name> plus one LF. If any exact container ID was ever adopted, exact-ID absence with the same byte rule and cleanup exit zero are also mandatory. Cleanup proof applies to every sealed classification; failure leaves C present and R absent.

result_seal.manifest: artifact-manifest.sha256 hashes every regular run artifact, including dotfiles, except itself and result-seal.json. Before manifest creation every entry is enumerated without delimiter splitting and nonregular/newline-named objects reject. VALID additionally requires the exact artifact filename set.
result_seal.receipt: run-receipt.json is one canonical object with exact classification, exits, cleanup, timing, identities, and file hashes.
result_seal.machine_rule: The hash-bound result validator and all candidate commit/tree/blob checks must pass before R is created. After the all-zero-old-value result-ref CAS, normal completion performs exact R topology, tree, local-byte identity, and validator replay before success. If a signal interrupts recovery, exact loose-ref observation yields exit 76 rather than a false R-absent claim; later independent full recovery decides the sealed classification. R has sole parent C.

canonical_test_result.rule: Require exact 0,0,0 pipeline status, one canonical JSON value, exact keys/events, integral bounded counters, empty details/stderr, exit-state agreement, OOM false, proved cleanup, complete artifacts, and immutable result seal.
canonical_test_result.interpretation: Development evidence for the exact public-core behavior only; not an experiment, relation, curve-family result, scaling estimate, rho comparison, or ECDLP improvement.

rules: Every GO receipt is one canonical LF-terminated jq -cS object with exact keys, role ID/path, and no findings.
Every principal is a nonzero UUID outside the 69 exclusions and pairwise distinct; authenticity remains externally trusted.
Every topology, tree, raw delta, mode, digest, image, and inventory fact is exact.
Any defect yields REVISE and no GO artifact.

authorization_decision_schema.required_interpretation: One isolated public development-test run only; no registered seed, campaign, experiment, scaling, rho, or ECDLP-improvement authority.

theory: Does V12 preserve exact five-test loading, Python isolation/origin checks, and development-only interpretation?
Does canonical authorization or result sealing alter any protected source/test contract?
Are result classifications and theorem boundaries exact under the trusted model?
accounting: Are whole-host and per-operation bounds, global file caps, protected resource counters, fixed overhead disclosure, complete inventories, exact cleanup receipts, and result sealing sufficient?
Does the C/R ref topology distinguish preconsumption, present-unvalidated, incomplete, and sealed outcomes mechanically without requiring full signal-time recovery?
Does the valid artifact set and immutable manifest cover every mandatory write without circularity?
red_team: Can any local filter/hook/config execute before trust, or can duplicate/noncanonical authorization JSON or LF-suffixed strings false-pass?
Can CREATE_PENDING, raw Docker acknowledgement bytes, signal/EXIT recovery, exact-ID ownership, cleanup, inventory, manifest, or result-ref logic be raced or forged inside the model?
Can any missing/extra artifact, extra JSON, fractional counter, cache object, sidecar, timeout ambiguity, or post-run mutation false-pass as valid?

go_no_go.go: Three fresh exact GO receipts, canonical four-file A directly on P, exact bootstrap substitution, absent run/C/R, empty complete inventories, pinned tools/image, no replacements/grafts/filter commands/info attributes.
go_no_go.no_go: Any REVISE, mismatch, token residue, noncanonical JSON, forbidden path, existing run/ref, tool/image drift, replacement/graft/filter/archive-command state, or inability to prove cleanup before a terminal seal leaves execution unauthorized or incomplete with C present and R absent.
go_no_go.next_action_after_go: Invoke the exact bootstrap once, preserve C/R and the complete run directory, independently interpret the sealed result, then design a separate registered-seed experiment.
